sections.title: What white-label SEO pricing includes
sections.body: A quote may cover discovery, research, recommendations, implementation, verification, meetings, revisions or client-facing presentation. These are separate responsibilities. Ask providers to state which are included and which require a new scope.

sections.title: Questions that move the price
sections.body: Discuss site count, page count, markets, languages, platform, access quality, migration risk, research depth, turnaround, review rounds and reporting format. The same label can describe materially different work.

sections.title: Model your own resale effort
sections.body: Your price must account for account management, quality assurance, client presentation, approvals, implementation coordination and risk. A partner quote is one input, not the complete cost of serving the client.

sections.title: Use public prices carefully
sections.body: VANTFLOW audit offers at $99 and $149 describe bounded public products. They are not standing white-label rates. Partner terms depend on responsibility, access, cadence, turnaround and presentation requirements.

sections.title: Compare like with like
sections.body: Ask whether revisions, urgent work, meetings, implementation checks, source files, reporting and post-release verification are included. A lower number is not comparable when it omits work your agency must later perform.

sections.title: Put assumptions beside deliverables
sections.body: A responsible proposal names exclusions, dependencies, review owners, deadlines and change triggers. This protects the agency’s margin and gives the client conversation a clear basis when new information appears.

cta.title: Discuss a scope before discussing partner terms
